description.narrative: 1) In July 2021, MOLE has established a Child Labor Unit (CLU) in BAARM to manage, implement and coordinate child labour- related work and advocacies in the BAARM region with the support of ministries such as the Ministry of Social Services and Development; Ministry of Basic, Higher and Technical Education; - Ministry of Trade, Investment and Tourism; Ministry of Agriculture; Fisheries and Agrarian Reform; and social partners. 2) Strengthened capacity of MOLE, particularly newly established Child Labor unit. Training Manual on Child Labour and its Laws, Policies and Programmes in the Philippines developed for use in BARMM. Training of trainers conducted in July 2021 to roll-out the use of Manual. (3) The National Council Against Child Labor submitted its action pledge for the International Year on the Elimination of Child Labour. (1) With RBSA support, the ILO provided technical and financial support to the WDACL activities in 2020 at national level. ILO also actively participated in the activities through social media and the judging of various contests that were designed by the National Council Against Child Labour. In WDACL 2021, ILO provided support as resource persons in various webinars. With support from Japan, in BARMM, ILO supported MOLE on the planning and holding of the WDACL event in 2021, including in the production of materials on the Sagip Batang Mangagawa (SBM), and facilitated the participation of the national DOLE Bureau of Workers with Special Concerns to the event. 2) With support from Japan, ILO conducted a technical meeting with the Minister and technical staff where CLU was discussed. The Minister designated the Deputy Minister and the head of SBM to serve as Focal Person for CLU and to work closely with ILO in the development of the CL unit. Copies of the CL related documents e.g. TORs of CL Focal Person etc were also shared with MOLE. In the light of COVID restriction, a group chat was created on Facebook to facilitate exchanges of data and information relative to CL. In July 2021, ILO conducted a training cum field testing of the training manual on child labour adapted for BARMM. 3 labour inspectors and 5 field officers along with heads of bureaus and offices of MOLE participated in the training. Core trainors from the group will help in the rolling out in provincial areas and local partners. Once finalized, MOLE particularly the SBM unit will use the CL Manual in their advocacy and training with the constituents in 2021 (last quarter). (3) The ILO made a presentation on Alliance 8.7 and the International Year on the Elimination of Child Labour to the National Council Against Child Labor which led to the submission of the government's action pledge for the International Year.

description.narrative:
The Online Post-Arrival Orientation Seminar was launched by the Philippine Overseas Labor Office in Hong Kong (China) in October 2020, providing OFWs access to relevant and reliable information in Hong Kong (China). This supported Department of Labour and Employment (DOLE) Order 532 (series of 2018) on creating post-arrival platforms and content for OFWs (result links to HKG901).
Filipino domestic workers in Hong Kong (China) underwent basic leadership training (36 Filipino women) and basic orientation seminar (240 Filipino women) in collaboration with the Progressive Labor Union of Domestic Workers-Hong Kong (PLUDW-HK), an affiliate of SENTRO (result links to HKG901).
Migrant resource centers (MRCs) in Negros Occidental province and Tabaco City (Albay Province) are now providing gender-responsive essential services to departing and returning Overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs) and families, especially women. Services include including case management, reintegration referrals, networking and organizing of OFW organizations, and capacity-building and leadership for women. In 2020-21 8,290 OFWs, of which 4,056 women, were supported with direct services, referrals, information and training services.
The Psychosocial Support and Task Force formed in 2020 and comprising government partners, trade unions, recruiters association, civil society, and volunteer licenses psychologists continues to provide online psychosocial first aid, counselling and referrals to OFWs especially women.
Babaeng BiyaHero campaign reached more than 4.8 million unique persons and generated more than 74 million impressions in various mass media and social media platforms. Its mobile app and information kiosks are located at Manila international airports.
TESDA is providing technical vocational skills development and reintegration support programs, through which 350 OFW scholars earned TESDA national skills certificate/training certificate on IT/STEM courses and other TVET skills. With support of the Government of Switzerland, ILO developed and piloted the Post-Arrival Orientation Seminar programme in Hong Kong (China) to enhance Filipino domestic workers' access to reliable and accurate information. ILO technically supported the development of Basic leadership and orientation services in collaboration with SENTRO for Filipino domestic workers in Hong Kong(FAIR II). ILO also supported the testing of case management tools and techniques to encourage Filipino domestic workers to pursue their cases after returning from Hong Kong.
ILO, with support of the European Union, enhanced design of programmes and operations and strengthened services for Overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs) (especially women and migrant domestic workers) of local governments, help desks, one-stop service centers, and Migrant Resource Centers.. 1500 stakeholder representatives trained on women's rights, gender and migration, promoting gender equality, reintegration and employment options for women OFWs.
The ILO supported the design of the public awareness and outreach campaign in the Philippines, in consultation with tripartite-plus partners. The key objectives are to raise awareness of migrant workers, policy makers, youth and Philippine public, and change public attitudes on women OFWs, VAW, Philippine migration issues; deepen understanding on risks and particular situation of women MWS, and the voice, choice, capacity/agency of women OFWs and their contributions in the Philippines and countries of destination.
ILO is providing technical and capacity support in running the collaborative #WOMENOFWSCANDOIT scholarship and technical vocational skills development and reintegration support programme. ILO has supported the conceptualizing and development of the "OFW Reintegration Advisor and Pathway Referrals" which provides an operational process flow and digital portal to assist OFWs on their reintegration in the Philippines.

description.narrative:
The Philippines Overseas Employment Administration (POEA) adopted a "Communication Plan" that employs social media action plan and strategies, based on ILO General Principles and Operational Guidelines on Fair Recruitment. The Communication Plan will operationalize communication strategies into a work plan with emphasis on promoting awareness and strengthening effective channels engagement with POEA's constituents.
The Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA) issued Memorandum Circular 32 Series of 2021 to pilot a zero-cost blended training programme for outbound migrant domestic workers that reduced in-person training from 28 days to 2 days, with online training modules (contact-less, 10 days) conducted by an ILO implementing partner.
The Philippine Congress incorporated recommendations from tripartite-plus consultations to adopt three new pieces of legislation including: 1. House Bill 6779 on mandatory immunization of overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs). The revised draft removed mandatory/forced immunization of OFWs as prerequisite to deployment, and included giving OFW priority access to COVID -19 vaccinations. 2. Senate Bill 2234 on creation of Department of Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos (DMWOF). A joint statement of at least 50 trade unions and migrant organizations was submitted to the Senate. The updated text incorporate key comments of ILO and stakeholders to strengthen reference to ILS and gender provisions. 3. Senate Bill 2088 on "Gender-Responsive and Inclusive Pandemic and Disaster Management Act" was approved by the Senate Gender and Women Committee in July 2021. The unity bill was sponsored by all women senators. It is aligned with ILS, gender equality and health standards.
The National Employment Recovery Strategy (NERS) labor sector agenda includes a migrant workers component (land-based, sea-based) that covers reintegration and employment support and social protection coverage for OFWs especially women. With support of the Government of Switzerland, ILO provided policy advice to the Philippines Overseas Employment Administration (POEA) to ensure that the Rules and Regulations forbidding the collection of recruitment fees to domestic workers are efficiently implemented through POEA social media platform.
ILO, with support of the Government of Switzerland, supported the design, monitoring and enforcement mechanisms of the online skills training programme, which was taken up by TESDA to implement actions to ensure that recruitment fees are not collected illegally through alternative training delivery and revised assessment requirements. ILO supported consultation with social partners.
With assistance from Government of Switzerland and the European Union, ILO participated in Senate Committee hearings and submitted Statements on the proposed Department of Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos, highlighting need to strengthen reference to ILS and gender provisions. The Senate Bill on Gender-Responsive and Inclusive Pandemic and Disaster-Management Act" was formulated through initiative of ILO after stakeholders' consultations.
ILO supported the National Employment Recovery Strategy (NERS) Task Force in holding stakeholder consultations to formulate the Labor Sector Agenda for NERS. Throughout the policy formulation process, ILO has supported the social partners' advocacy programmes and strategies and promoted the inclusion of Overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs), especially women and migrant domestic workers, in universal health care and social protection coverage (health care, OSH compensation, unemployment benefits, retirement, provident savings, etc.) in the Philippines.
